text:
Kent Johnson has gone from a depth role to a featured one in Columbus. He is at 18:07 a night, up from 13:14, on the ice for 80% of the power play, and he has 18 points in 18 games after 0.29 a game last season. Our wins-added ranks him 12th of 530 skaters. The Athletic also noted his numbers make him the league's top shootout artist.

The role change is the real part. His own chances are up to 0.99 expected goals per 60 from 0.69, and he has 13 points in his last ten games. The finishing is the part to discount: eight goals on 5.4 expected, shooting 19% after 6% last season, and a points pace of 3.31 per 60 that sits far above his talent range.

What to watch is the five-on-five work. Columbus gets 48.17% of expected goals at 5v5 with him on, roughly what it gets without him, and Evolving-Hockey had the offense drying up with him on the ice last season. Columbus has lost four straight, with a point from him in three. Eighteen games is a small sample, but the minutes say the coaches believe it.
headline: Kent Johnson's breakout is mostly real
